name: Sofia Airport
before:
Bulgaria's main international airport, 10 km east of central Sofia. It passed 8 million passengers for the first time in 2025.

It is the home base for Bulgaria Air, BH Air, European Air Charter and GullivAir, and a base for both Ryanair and Wizz Air, which is what keeps fares to Sofia low.

The infrastructure is more modern than the airport's reputation suggests. A completely new runway system opened on 31 August 2006, replacing facilities described as old and out of date. The 3,600 metre runway sits 210 metres north of the old one, with its eastern end carried over the bed of the Iskar river on a purpose-built structure. A new 50 metre control tower followed in December 2012.

The airport also houses a Bulgarian Air Force base.
after:
Bulgaria's main international airport, 10 km east of central Sofia. It passed 8 million passengers for the first time in 2025.

Bulgaria Air, the national airline, flies its regular routes from here. Ryanair also has a base.

Its runway is 3,600 metres long. The airport also houses a Bulgarian Air Force base, Vrazhdebna.
